title: Mixture-of-RAG: Integrating Text and Tables with Large Language Models

problem.claim: Real-world documents often combine extensive narrative content with complex hierarchical tables, requiring retrieval and reasoning across both modalities.

gap.claim: Existing RAG systems perform worse when processing heterogeneous text-table hierarchies.

contributions.claim: MixRAG is a three-stage framework combining hierarchy row-and-column-level representation, ensemble retrieval with LLM-based reranking, and multi-step reasoning decomposition using RECAP prompting.
The authors release DocRAGLib, a 2k-document corpus paired with automatically aligned text-table summaries and gold document annotations.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors explicitly describe MixRAG as a novel framework.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that MixRAG improves top-1 retrieval by 46% over strong text-only, table-only, and naive-mixture baselines.
The authors report new state-of-the-art performance for mixed-modality document grounding.

narrative_sequence.summary: LLM responses benefit from grounding in external knowledge sources.
Real-world documents combine narrative text with hierarchically structured tables, while existing RAG performance deteriorates on such heterogeneous structures.
The work formalizes Heterogeneous Document RAG as joint retrieval and reasoning over textual and hierarchical tabular data.
The authors introduce MixRAG and release the DocRAGLib dataset.
The authors report a 46% top-1 retrieval improvement and state-of-the-art performance for mixed-modality document grounding.

source_observation.claim: The proposed framework represents hierarchical structure, combines multiple retrieval strategies, and decomposes reasoning for documents containing both text and tables.

interpretation.claim: Multimodal retrieval quality may depend on preserving document structure and coordinating retrieval with reasoning.

application.claim: Systems that answer questions over mixed narrative and tabular documents could consider structure-aware representations, reranking, and staged reasoning.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether these design choices generalize beyond the reported document-grounding setting.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the evaluation datasets, metrics beyond top-1 retrieval, or experimental protocol.
The abstract does not provide implementation details, ablations, error analysis, or independent verification of the reported results.
